title: Airfare of the Week: Royal Brunei Business Class Jakarta – Melbourne from $2,085
body:
Australian Frequent Flyer
Australian Frequent Flyer - Tips, Tricks and Chat for Australian Frequent Flyers
Melbourne, Australia. Photo: Matt Graham.
Our newest Airfare of the Week belongs to Royal Brunei Airlines, which has round-trip Business Class fares from Jakarta (CGK) to Melbourne (MEL) from $2,085.
While Royal Brunei isn’t part of any alliance, this fare could still be useful for integrating into a return trip to Asia.
Here are the full details of this great Business Class airfare from Jakarta to Melbourne.
Sample itinerary & pricing
Example pricing. Screenshot from Royal Brunei website.
You can book this fare directly on the Royal Brunei website . The fare is priced at IDR26,479,100 (~AU$2,085).
Note that fares and availability are subject to change. This fare may not be available by the time you read this article, and you might need to be flexible with travel dates. We recommend booking ASAP to avoid disappointment!
Travel dates & fare rules
Here are the details of this airfare:
Maximum stay at the destination of 12 months
One free stopover permitted, plus unlimited additional stopovers at USD50 (~AU$70) each. No stopover can exceed 14 days
Change fee: IDR700,000 (~AU$55)
Cancellation fee: IDR1,400,000 (~AU$111)
On-board product
Royal Brunei flies the Airbus A320neo from Jakarta to Bandar Seri Begawan. This is a standard narrow-body recliner-style product in a 2-2 layout.
For its flights from Bandar Seri Begawan to Melbourne, the airline flies a Boeing 787 equipped with 18 lie-flat Business Class seats.
A Royal Brunei 787-8 at Melbourne Airport. Photo: Matt Graham.
These seats are in a 2-2-2 configuration. A seat in the middle pair would best suit solo travellers as these have direct aisle access.
Note that Royal Brunei is a dry airline and doesn’t serve alcohol on board.
Earning points & status credits with this airfare
This fare books into “D” class. As Royal Brunei doesn’t partner with any other airline frequent flyer program, you can only earn miles in its own Royal Skies program. The “D” class earns at 150%, resulting in a total of 13,410 Royal Skies miles.
You would need 32,500 miles for a saver one-way Economy Class award from Melbourne to Brunei. However, flight redemptions start from 8,000 miles for shorter sectors. You can also use miles for seat selection, lounge access, upgrades and extra baggage.
